utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, let us continue where we left off yesterday. I believe that your last answer was actually the explanation that you gave to us about Witness VG117's description of her husband; that is, you remembered her husband and you told us that you knew him as a customer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So it was according to her description, Mr. Vasiljevic, that you were able to remember her husband, in particular, thanks to the detail concerning her brother. Can you remember, at the time you waited on him when he was a customer in your restaurant, did he come with his wife or alone?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited on him several times, but I really cannot remember him being with his wife on any of these occasions. I really cannot remember any such occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: One more question, Mr. Vasiljevic, about the restaurant located in the vicinity of the Visegrad market. Is there a restaurant there that would have been closer to the market in Visegrad, that is, closer than the Panos restaurant?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very entrance to the market, there are two or three such establishments, catering facilities, and there was the Borke restaurant, in the direction of the Panos restaurant, and two smaller cafes before the Panos restaurant, if you're going from the market towards the restaurant. Let me also mention that all these places were significantly cheaper than our restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, if you remember the testimony of VG117, you will probably recall that she mentioned that when you were working in the restaurant, that you would sometimes address her, that you would greet her, exchange a couple of words. She also said that you would greet her by using her maiden name. I'm not going to mention it, because she is a protected witness, but you will probably remember that surname. Is that correct, what the Witness VG117 said?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I really couldn't remember waiting on her at all. I mean, I cannot say that I -- for sure that I never, ever waited on her, because, after all, I worked there for about 17 years, but I really cannot remember her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Finally, you heard her testimony here before the Court when she said that there was a person who was registering people in front of the Vuk Karadzic school on behalf of the Red Cross organisation, and she identified that person as being you, Mitar Vasiljevic. Did you personally have any idea as to whom she might have been referring to? Because it is your testimony that it was not you. If such an individual did exist, do you have any idea who that might be?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I was listening to the testimony of VG117, I thought about it, and it occurred to me that it could perhaps have been Stanimir Zilic, also known as Crni, because I know that he used to work at the Red Cross organisation, so I thought that she may have mistaken him for me and hence gave such a comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, the evidence so far is that he wasn't working for the Red Cross at that time. I'm not sure what the value of this piece of evidence is anyway. You're asking the accused to speculate. He doesn't know. We've had two people now who are suggested to be alike to him in appearance, and there was no suggestion that this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: We have no translation, Your Honour. We have no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, dear. Well, I'll start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It's my mistake. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: My point is this: The evidence so far is this man Zilic was not there at the time. He didn't work for the Red Cross at that time. And really, you're only asking your client to speculate. I don't see that it helps us very much for him to say, "Well, it might have been Mr. Zilic." You could certainly ask him whether people have mistaken him for Zilic or Zilic for him, or something like that, but this doppelganger point that you raised before doesn't seem to have come to any fruition. It's a matter for you, but I really don't think that your client's guess will assist us very much on this point. The real issue is whether there was anybody there on behalf of the Red Cross. Now, the evidence that you have led so far is that there was not. And that's a matter which we can take into account. It's a -- your client's point is that he was in hospital at the time. And that's really all he can say of his own knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was able to establish that indeed Mr. Zilic did not work for the Red Cross at that time. So I'm not trying to show that. However, we tried to identify a person whom we thought might have worked for the Red Cross. Mr. Vasiljevic thought about him, because he knew that he had worked for the Red Cross, but he didn't know that he was not working for the Red Cross at that time. That is the reason why we didn't even want to bring him as a witness. It is not our case that the individual in question worked for the Red Cross at the time. However, in view of what we emphasised sometime ago and promised that we would try to find that person, because we believe that such a person existed, I asked the question that I just asked. That was the reason for my question. Mr. Stanimir Zilic, according to the witness, had started working for the Red Cross at one point in time, but he was not a Red Cross employee at this time. This was my last question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, we've heard quite a bit about how you may or may not have known this woman and how well you may have known her, but the truth of the matter is when that woman walked into this courtroom or into the other courtroom, you recognised her, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, it's -- it's like this: I really don't know the woman by her name and surname, nor did I know that she was the wife of the person I mentioned. I never knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not asking you whether you knew her name. What I'm asking you is, when she entered the courtroom just before testifying, did you not recognise her as somebody that you had seen before in your life? Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How shall I put it? I don't know exactly. If I were to see her in the street, I wouldn't recognise her as a person from Visegrad. I don't know what to tell you. Of course now I have an idea of the -- I know the family she belongs to because I used to know her father, and she has somewhat similar features.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, let's be clear. So your testimony here today is when that woman walked into the courtroom, you did not recognise her and you did not recognise her until such time as she began to describe features about where she was born and her family. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you should have asked me where she was from before she gave her testimony, I wouldn't have known that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, she describes seeing you on the bus back to the area where you both come from. Is it a fact that you from time to time would take the bus from Visegrad up to your home village of Djurdevici to visit family?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall ever seeing this woman on the bus travelling to the same area to visit her family?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were seven bus lines; that's what she said. There was only one bus, one service, that we used and only one road that this bus took. Whether I saw her ever or not, it's very hard to say. Many people take the same bus. I'm not trying to exclude any such possibility. That was, as I said, the only service for this particular village, for the village of Zupa, and we all took that bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, at this time I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution document number 130. It's a map of the villages that we've heard testimony about. The top four copies have a little green Post-it, just to orient everybody's attention to the part of the map that I will be dealing with. I would ask that the Bench and the accused be given the top four copies. I ran out of Post-its.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's nice to think that we get a privileged copy for once, Mr. Groome. But you better show Mr. Domazet a copy so that he can tell us whether he objects to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's on the upper left-hand corner of the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you any objection to the tender of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It will be Exhibit P130.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, I would draw your attention to the top left-hand corner. Djurdevici is just above where I've put that green sticker.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I know the Defence received one with a sticker. Perhaps after Mr. Domazet is oriented, we could trade copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look above the green sticker. Can you see the village of Djurdevici there?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to remove the green sticker now and to take the blue pen in front of you. I'd ask you to draw a circle around your village.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask you just to put your initials inside that circle to indicate that that's your village.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask you to draw a circle around the village of VG117, the village that you went to school for your first four years. You can still use the blue marker.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't see very well. But I'll -- I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: While that's being done, Mr. Groome, can you orient us in relation to this top map. Where are we in relation to Visegrad? It's hard to pick up on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you -- actually, I just put the second page for the scale, for the legend. So it is not a continuation. But if you travel down the river, down towards the bottom of the map, along the right-hand side of the river, you will see Kosovo Polje, which is a place that we've heard about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG117 talked about her -- I'm sorry. Can you tell us where your family's property was, if it wasn't in the village. Could you circle that on the map, if it's a different place than what you circled already.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I will be able to orient myself precisely on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, if you're not sure, before --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately. But again, I'm not sure. Here, in this part, in this area more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And it looks like you've drawn a dot. Does that dot represent where your property is?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this line means between these two places. I know where Josovici [phoen] is, Nikolici, but this is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us how far a walk is it from the village of Djurdevici to your family's property?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, up to this property here, above, 30 to 40 minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So to --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe less. Maybe less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So to walk from your village to your family's property would be perhaps 30 to 40 minutes or perhaps a little less; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you're certain about where a location is, then I'll ask you to mark the map. If you're uncertain, let's not have you mark the map. We'll just have you -- I'll ask you to describe where you believe it is. Is your property in the direction of VG117's village?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where this point is, is the area where Serb properties are located, and beneath the village of Witness VG117 are Muslim properties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to indicate again for us where -- what you've just told us. Would you indicate -- it's now on the overhead projector, so we can all see it. Can you please indicate where the Muslim properties were and where the Serb properties were.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These here would be Serb properties. I don't know what this line stands for. And below this village there are Muslim properties. My village would have been here, on the Drina, and then here, in this part. This is the area where the Serb properties were, and further up are Muslim properties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The dot that you've drawn, is that your best estimate of where the Vasiljevic family property is?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my property, my personal property, or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The property that belongs to your family, that you as a child would go to and you would tend cattle there. Is that what you represented when you drew the dot?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many Serb properties here in the area where my property is located. I cannot pinpoint the exact location of my property. All I want to tell you is that this is the area where Serb properties are located, and my property was also there, and further up is the area where Muslim properties are. Now, maybe here, more or less. I really cannot pinpoint the exact spot. I'm not well versed in these matters. This must be the creek, the brook, coming from the village above, this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you to make a few marks on this map and then we'll be finished. Would you draw a circle to indicate where the Serb properties are. And if you would write "Serb" in your own language in that circle.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just draw a line like this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it will be very precise, but I think that it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As best you're able.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really -- I apologise, but I have to ask you: This straight black line, does it represent the brook?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't know that --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going -- or coming from the village above?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you're not able to tell us, Mr. Vasiljevic, then I won't ask you to make marks. If you're able, then I will ask you. If you feel you can make a mark where the Serb properties are, then I'd ask you to do so. If you cannot, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. It's not the stream in question. This must be a road. No. I'm sure I'm going to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you're sure you're going to make a mistake, please do not mark the map, Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really afraid that I'll make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. VG117 said the name of her family's property was Jela, or J-e-l-a. Are you familiar with that place?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say, sorry? Jela?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG117 said the property that her family owned was called Jela, J-e-l-a. Do you know where the property that is referred to as that name, that area, is located?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I know that my property is called Kadarici [phoen]. Jela doesn't ring a bell. I don't know. But the way names are given to properties is -- for example, if I have three or four meadows in the area of Kadarici, each one of them would have a name, but that is probably how her family referred to their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd just ask you to finish up with this diagram, or this map. Would you put "117" to indicate where the village is that 117 came from, and would you just write your name somewhere on the map so we know that it's your work.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the village of Witness 117. I am referring to the entire area of the village. I think that they would go in the direction of this village. I'm not going to mention the name of the village. If this is the entire area, I mean, her hamlet would have been here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We can't see what you're doing. You've drawn a circle to represent her village. Would you simply put the number 117 next to it to indicate that that's what you meant when you drew that circle.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the circle?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Anywhere near the circle is fine.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And if you would just write your name somewhere on the map - anywhere is fine - so that -- down from your other markings.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we've now got, I think, four dots, haven't we? Are there any of those that you want to have marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Given the imprecise -- or his statement that he is sure that he was making a mistake, I think it's perhaps best that we disregard those four dots, given the imprecision involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. So we've got his initials beside the top one and "117" and "MV" written in the other circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm finished with the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I just have a couple of more questions for you. How long would it take you, as a child, to walk from your village to the school in VG117's village?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. There was a break in interpretation, but I think I do understand your question. You're asking me how much time I needed to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. reach the village of Witness 117 from my village?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, from your home.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village where I was born?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm asking you: How long would it take you to walk to school as a boy? Give us an approximation of that.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would take me one hour, because it's a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And am I correct in thinking that for at least four years of your life, you were in VG117's village every day that school was open, give or take some days that you might have been sick? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. I'll add some information. I never passed through -- they're separate here. There's a little hamlet here. I never passed through that hamlet when I was going to school. They're separate, and very much so. I won't mention the name of this hamlet, but I never passed through here, never through the hamlet. There, to the right, towards this village here, the one above.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The hamlet that you say -- or that VG117 lived in, was it closer to your home or further away from your home than the actual village that VG117 would have -- would have been the closest village to her hamlet?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's parallel. It's like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So please don't --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see -- my village is here, and it's like this. So you'd go this way and this way. So it's more or less in this direction, if you go as the bird flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be approximately the same distance from your home?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately, but you wouldn't take the same route she would go to my home. She wouldn't go from here, where I went to school. She wouldn't go from the school to my home, but she would go from here to my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to be clear on what your testimony is here today. Is it your testimony -- let's assume that perhaps in your mind, VG117 is mistaken about the date. Is it your testimony that you never were in front of that school on any day recording the names of people and representing yourself to be the Red Cross? Is that your testimony? Forget the date for a second. I'll ask you that in my next question.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me whether I was ever in front of that school during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At any time were you in front of that school, writing people's names down in a book?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Never. Never, sir. Believe me. I've told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And we know from before where you say you were on the 22nd of June. In the hospital; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vasiljevic, I would like to return to the last question of Mr. Groome concerning the school to which you went. Given your explanation that the place of this witness's home is at the same distance from the school, my question will be precise. Did you go -- on the way to the school, did you pass near the house in which the family of this witness lived?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My village is here. This is the witness's village. The school is here in the village, so that means that I would take this route. I apologise, the school is below this pass. I haven't marked it, but it doesn't matter. So I'd go from here to school. And the witness in the hamlet -- when I wanted to get from this village to the hamlet, I wouldn't take the route that I used to go to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have understood you, but I just want to know that in your opinion, what is the distance from the pass that you used to go to school to the hamlet in which the family of the witness lived, the nearest way?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about 1 kilometre from the school. But I never -- I could never go through her hamlet, never, because it doesn't lead there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: One of Mr. Groome's questions concerned the bus trip to Djurdevici. Djurdevici is the place you were born in, but you lived in Visegrad, you said. How often or how many times did you go to the village of Djurdevici?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the village of where I was born very often. I went by boat, by car sometimes when I had a friend. I also went there by bus. But what she has said, that we met on the bus, I mean that's not interesting. I don't know what's interesting about it. That's the line that we have to use. There are about 50 or 60 passengers on the bus at all times. And I can say that for each person who is from that area. I don't know. I've visited my family. It's the only route.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, apart from other ways that you could have used to go to the village, by the Drina or by boat or by car with a friend, if we're talking about a bus trip, can you remember more or less how many times in the course of the year, on average, you went to the village by bus?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that in summer I went more often, but not by bus. When I worked in the fields in the winter, I would sometimes not go there for two months or three, because my father often came -- or came to the town more often, so we would see each other there. But I can't really tell you how many times exactly. How do I know? I was born there. There are various kombis. I didn't always have to go by bus. Sometimes with a friend. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Good. I won't insist on that, then. It might be difficult to reply to this at the moment. A few more questions about these villages that you have marked. Perhaps it will have some importance. Your village of Djurdevici, was it a Serbian village or was it a mixed village? Did both Muslims and Serbs live there?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My village was exclusively inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And the other village that you have marked as the place in which the family of the witness lived?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims alone. Muslims alone, a hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And another thing: Could you have a look at the map that you've been given by the Prosecutor and try to find the place called Velika Gorica and to circle this place. Could you mark it in some way. Would you -- do you need glasses perhaps? Well, if you had something, perhaps mine would serve, because obviously he has some problems. If you have found it, could you please circle it. Could you mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We have another colour, which may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, maybe. Definitely better.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you mark "117" - below it - "-2" as the place where she was married and where she lived, the witness.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what is it that is written underneath it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should state "117-2." But I agree that it's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's all right. As long as we've got it recorded on the transcript. Thank you. That's the end? Thank you, Mr. Vasiljevic. You can return to your usual seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that the conclusion of your case in response to the reopening of the Crown -- of the Prosecution case?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, as far as the witness is concerned. But there are a few more written exhibits that I would like to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above all, I'm not sure about this map, if Mr. Groome doesn't suggest that it be entered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is. It is Exhibit P130. You did agree to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Very well. I have -- I would suggest that this certificate be entered as evidence, from the company Panos, of the 23rd of January, 2002. I have a translation of this. And it concerns evidence that this company has - about records this company has about the fact that Vasiljevic, Mitar -- it has evidence about the restaurants in which Vasiljevic, Mitar worked and also that he never worked in the hotel Vilina Vlas. I will provide you with the originals and photocopies in B/C/S and English. I will provide a significant number of copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you give a copy to Mr. Groome on the way, I think it will save a significant amount of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet has given me one before we started this morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you any objection to the tender of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm looking for my list of numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is D50, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, D50 and D50.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. D50 and D50.1. I may have got the wrong impression yesterday, Mr. Domazet, but I thought that your client did say he actually did at times fill in at the -- at the hotel that -- the Vilina Vlas hotel, but he didn't work there regularly. It may have been a wrong impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It was for restaurant Panos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: He was talking about restaurant Panos, not for restaurant in hotel Vilina Vlas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the new arrangements are such that we haven't got our new transcript yet. The Registry seems to think that we should be pressing buttons rather than CLSS about the transcript these days, and it hasn't yet appeared electronically. So I can't check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second exhibit is a letter from the Red Cross, the organisation in Visegrad, of the 23rd of January, 2002 at the request -- in response to the Defence request for lists, any lists, of documents on the parties of convoys in 1992. We received an answer which we are going to provide in B/C/S and in English. And in this answer, it states that they don't have any such documents because all the documents were destroyed on the 19th of 1996 when, in the neighbouring offices, a bomb was placed and everything was destroyed, and the documents were destroyed, too. So I would ask you to enter this as Exhibit D59 -- 51. D51.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. They will be Exhibit D51 and D51.1. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And further, Your Honour, in the proceedings of disclosing documents by Mr. Groome, I received an expert report from the institute, from the Dutch institute, on the medical documents and on the case history, and this exhibit -- I have received this exhibit, and it hasn't been entered as an exhibit by the Prosecutor, so I have entered it as a potential exhibit, and I would ask this to be entered as Defence Exhibit under the number D52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there an English version or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. It's only an English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. No objection, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to any of the reports done by the Dutch Forensic Institute. There was that other matter of the radiologist from the Dutch hospital that we talked about. So I don't have a copy of what we're actually entering into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you'd better have a look at it. I think it's all the attempts the Prosecution made to challenge the veracity of the hospital records.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. That will be Exhibit D52. There is some material at the back, which I think are the documents themselves, which we probably have English versions of somewhere, I hope. Do we, Mr. Domazet? These are the documents which were tested, you see. They're at the back of the report. Are they already all in English -- all in evidence, with English versions of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour. There is a translation. It's the case history, and it has been translated into English. This is in the Serbian language, et al., the matter referring to the expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They do look familiar, but I just wanted to make sure that we do have English versions of them, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] One other matter, Your Honour. With the Exhibit 113A of the Prosecutor, which was submitted yesterday and which is only a partially amended finding, there was also a transcript which was submitted, which relates to the tape in dispute, for which the Prosecution says is a tape of the witness, of the protected witness, on page A, under 2250, which is where the transcript begins. In my opinion, there is also a problem in that my expert, Krstic, also noticed in his finding - and this is something that I personally verified - in this first sentence it says: "I think that Mitar, Mitar did quite a few things." If you listen to it carefully - and the expert also noticed this - instead of "did," it says "said," which, in the Defence's opinion, is very important, in case one should determine that this tape is reliable and should be an exhibit. And then thirdly, in the third line, where it says "Mitar," it says: [As interpreted] "I said I didn't know that, but I knew that he led the people to clean glasses." So in the English translation, it says "glasses." However, the real expression is "carsija," which is sort of a Turkish word, which is also used in the Serbian language and which means a town, the centre of a town. So carsija, town, is something quite different, whereas the translation, it says "glass," and in the B/C/S too is says "glass," which is illogical. If you listen to it very carefully, you can see that it says they are cleaning the carsija, the town. So I would like this to be verified and I would like this version of the translation to be corrected. Perhaps this part could also be shown here again, because I think the translators will find it easier -- the interpreters will find it easier to hear it and to interpret it. It's a matter of two minutes, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you arranged to have it played?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have this, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got it there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, it may be the safest way, although if you say it has to be listened to very carefully, the circumstances under which we have an instantaneous interpretation are hardly that. It may be best if we asked the CLSS to take it away and listen to it very carefully, which they can do, but not when it's being played here in Court, and then we can get a report from them in relation to those --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you should supply them with the translation we have at the moment and ask them -- indicate the particular parts that you want them to check and let them give us a report on it. That would be the simplest way of dealing with it and probably the most accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I agree. I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you any problem with that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would agree with that as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. We'll ask the CLSS to do that. But you had better supply them with the recording and with the transcript, with those two particular matters highlighted in some way. I can understand the second one seems to be obviously the correct -- what you suggested seems to be obviously correct. The first one, I'm not quite sure what significance you see in "he said many things" rather than "did many things." I saw nothing particular sinister in the interpretation that was already placed on it. But it's best that we have it correct, if we can. Well, now, apart from that, is there anything -- any other documents you want to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the exhibit that Mr. Groome -- yesterday or the day before yesterday, he spoke about this exhibit. It is the one about blood groups, which shows that the blood group of the accused, according to the investigation in the Scheveningen Detention Centre, is the same as the one in his medical history. He hasn't tendered this into evidence. I would suggest that this be done, but the only problem is that I don't have it here with me. I don't know whether Mr. Groome will personally suggest this. I would suggest this to be an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Funnily enough, it was filed, I think, because I have on my desk a copy of it as having been filed, and I wondered why on earth I had been given it until I realised -- I thought it was for some appointment he had over at the hospital, but it is dated last year and it does have a blood grouping on it. Perhaps it should be tendered formally rather than simply filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I raise this as a matter of fairness with Mr. Domazet to -- it seemed to be an appropriate Defence exhibit and it seemed to be a document that if I were sitting in judgement on this case I would want before me. So I brought Mr. Domazet's attention to these documents. Just before we started, I ran out to see if I could get copies for Mr. Domazet. They haven't come back. Perhaps we either can take a short break for me to get those copies for Mr. Domazet to tender or we can take care of it in terms of an agreement, and I'd be willing to agree that the blood result of the person in the Uzice hospital, their blood was typed as A with positive rhesus factor, and that Mr. Vasiljevic's blood, when it was tested in the Scheveningen prison, had the same blood type, A-plus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I am amazed that in this day and age please still use the old A/B/O blood grouping. It's so general in nature. But still, it's some evidence which Mr. Domazet can use. If it had been inconsistent, then there would have been something about it. Well, can you come to an agreement? Are you happy with that agreement that Mr. Groome has offered, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honour, that this is all right. If Mr. Groome and I agree with the blood group is A positive rhesus, and this was established in Scheveningen and in other medical examinations, so it won't have to be entered as a special exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we had yesterday some percentage given to us for A, Rh positive, and we can simply note that he forms one of the 30 something per cent of the population, as did the person in the hospital. Is that the lot now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. And just one other thing. Mr. Groome, in the course of the proceedings, submitted a calendar on Muslim religious holidays. I have a calendar of Orthodox holidays for 1992, which I also gave to Mr. Groome so that he could verify it, and I think it would be good to establish, on the basis of this calendar, two matters: that in 1992, on Sunday, the 14th of June, that day was an Orthodox holiday of the Holy Trinity, and on Sunday, the 28th of June, it is St. Vitus' Day. That's also an Orthodox holiday. And both of those holidays, according to the Orthodox calendar, are marked in red letters, in the calendar that I possess. The calendar for the month of June is being translated and you will have the original and the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's interesting how many of the religions depend upon red-letter days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I gather that your Serbian calendar is being translated for us. Do you want to actually tender it? We might as well have it, seeing we've got the Muslim one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D53. And when the translation comes, we'll distribute it. Is that your case now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Groome, have you got a case in reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the end of the evidence, then. We made an order on the 28th of January that the parties' final briefs are to be filed on the 25th of February. I remind you that you have been under notice since sometime in November that you would have to start preparing those briefs, so that is the reason for the shortness of the time. We also issued a list of issues upon which we sought the assistance of the parties. It may be that you've already, each of you, considered those particular issues, but we wanted to draw your attention to them particularly, because those are the matters where we see that we really do need some assistance. We, of course, have not made up our minds anywhere as to what the outcome of the case should be, but the particular prospect that the alibi succeeds, if I may state it wrongly as to an onus of proof, is a matter of some concern, because we would then have to know what the Prosecution case was as to particularly the accused's state of mind at the time he is alleged to have been shepherding people into the house in Pionirska Street. The order on the 28th of January also fixed the 5th and the 6th of March. That was after consultation with both of you. Are those days still suitable to you for the final addresses?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Suitable to the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How about you, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We look forward to seeing you on the 5th of March, and we will now adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.04 a.m.
